approachQuestion.prompt:
Sections still requiring patrol

A route has requested patrol sections A and sections B already checked by another team. Both lists contain half-open intervals, are sorted by start, and are internally separated with end[i] < start[i+1]. Return the sorted maximal half-open pieces covered by A but not by B. Do not modify either list. Empty pieces are omitted; sharing only an endpoint removes no length.

Input: A = [[1,10],[13,17]], B = [[0,3],[5,7],[9,15]]
Output: [[3,5],[7,9],[15,17]]

Input: A = [[2,4]], B = [[4,6]]
Output: [[2,4]]

Constraints: 0 ≤ m,n ≤ 200000 for the lengths of A,B; integer endpoints satisfy 0 ≤ start < end ≤ 1000000000. Inputs support indexed reads. Return new records. Prefer best worst-case time, then least auxiliary memory, excluding output.

options.text: Scan A in order with a cursor inside its current interval and a forward index in B. Skip B intervals ending at or before the cursor. For each B interval starting before the current A end, emit any gap before B, advance the cursor past the removed coverage, and advance B only if its end is at or before the current A end. Emit any remaining tail of A.
options.feedback: Both frontiers move forward. A B interval extending past one A interval is retained for the next A interval, so a single long checked section can remove several separated patrol sections.

options.text: For each A interval, scan all of B from the beginning and subtract each intersecting interval, emitting the surviving gaps in order.
options.feedback: This is correct but may repeatedly traverse almost all of B for each A interval. Sorted separated lists permit retaining a forward position instead of restarting.

options.text: Discard an entire A interval if it overlaps any B interval; otherwise return it unchanged.
options.feedback: For A=[[1,10]] and B=[[4,6]], the correct result is [[1,4],[6,10]]. Partial removal need not erase the whole requested section.

options.text: Use the forward cursor scan, but advance past every B interval as soon as it intersects any A interval.
options.feedback: For A=[[1,3],[5,7]] and B=[[0,6]], consuming B after the first A interval misses its removal of [5,6); the correct remaining piece is [6,7].

feedback.reason: Subtract ordered coverage while retaining a remover that spans several source intervals.
details: Track one index into each list and a cursor within the current A interval. Emit surviving pieces directly. Keep a B interval for later A intervals whenever it extends beyond the current A end; otherwise advance its index. Use an output array preallocated with capacity m+n and a logical length, without a trimming copy.

Subtracting one B range can split an A range. Retain B when it extends beyond the current A so later A ranges still see that exclusion. Emit survivors directly rather than materializing every overlap pair.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For subtract-monotone-frontiers, analyze worst-case time for nonempty lists of lengths m and n. The whole returned capacity m+n is output space. What is the tightest standard pair?
constraints: Analyze only the named method. Count all temporary arrays and the call stack; exclude the supplied input and returned output. Numeric comparisons, assignments and arithmetic take constant time, with no overflow.
No hashing or amortized data structure is used. All loops and binary searches are iterative; there is no recursive stack.

options.text: Time O((m+n) log(m+n)), auxiliary space O(1)

feedback.reason: Forward cursors and emitted pieces have linear total work across both lists.
details: Each A interval completes once; each B interval is skipped or consumed once. A retained B interval can be visited again only as another A interval completes, so the total remains linear. Subtracting n separated intervals creates at most m+n surviving pieces. Only indices and endpoint variables are auxiliary state.
Iterative monotone scan; preallocated returned output; no copies or sorting.
“Time O(mn), auxiliary space O(1)”: The B index does not restart for each A interval. Retaining a long B interval costs at most one revisit per completed A interval.
“Time O(m+n), auxiliary space O(m+n)”: The surviving pieces are returned output. No temporary list or input copy is created, so auxiliary memory is constant.
“Time O((m+n) log(m+n)), auxiliary space O(1)”: The two supplied lists are already ordered. The algorithm subtracts with forward indices and does not sort them.
